## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahābyūha Sutta* (Snp 4.13, PTS Snp 174) is a discourse within the fourth chapter (Aṭṭhakavagga) of the *Suttanipāta*, titled "The Longer Discourse on Arrayed For Battle" in English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. Its central theme concerns how one may preserve spiritual freedom within a world rife with disputes [SuttaCentral]. In modern studies examining whether the Aṭṭhakavagga suttas advocate release from rebirth, verse 902 of the sutta is highlighted as a rare passage explicitly touching on the theme, asking why one should tremble or desire anything when for them there is no passing away and reappearing (*cutūpapāto*) [Ruegg & Schmithausen 1990].

A canonical commentary is dedicated to the sutta in the *Mahāniddesa* under the title *Mahābyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 13) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects this close canonical relationship, showing 105 matching passages (9,766 shared characters) with Mnd 13, alongside reuse in the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records an early Chinese parallel to the sutta preserved in the *Arthapada Sūtra* (T 198) [SuttaCentral], though DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language algorithmic matches exceeding its threshold [DharmaNexus].
